title: Opt-in telemetry client
goal: Client side of opt-in telemetry: a typed, allow-list-only emitter that is off by default, honours DO_NOT_TRACK unconditionally, buffers locally and ships batches to POST /v1/telemetry/events without ever linking to a user account.
scope_in: Typed emit functions for exactly the CT-TELEMETRY v1 events: `app.start`, `app.exit`, `command.run {name}`, `session.created {mode, transport}`, `session.joined {transport}`, `agent.state_change {from,to}` (state enums only), `feature.used {key}`, `error.shown {code}`, `perf.startup {ms}`, `perf.frame {p95_ms}`, `update.result {from,to,ok}`.

Enablement gate `isEnabled()`: true only if config `telemetry.enabled` is true AND `DO_NOT_TRACK` is not `1` AND `CENTCOM_TELEMETRY` is not `off`. When false, emit calls are no-ops that allocate nothing and write nothing to disk.

Allow-list sanitiser: each field has a regex/enum (`name` matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9-]{0,31}$` and is checked against the CLI's registered command names; `key` matches `^[a-z][a-z0-9_.-]{0,47}$`; `from`/`to` must satisfy `isAgentWireState`; `code` must be an `ErrorCode`; `mode` in command_post|branch; `transport` in lan|relay); an event failing the allow-list is dropped and counted, never sent.

Random per-install `install_id` (ULID) persisted at `<state dir>/telemetry/install_id` (0600); `resetInstallId()` deletes and regenerates it (backs `centcom telemetry reset`); `telemetryStatus()` returns enabled flag, install_id presence, buffered count.
Bounded buffer: max 1000 events in memory, drop oldest first; batch <= 100 events and <= 64 KiB; at most one send per 60 s; flush on exit with a 2 s deadline.

Sender: `POST {api.base_url}/v1/telemetry/events` with `Idempotency-Key` (a fresh ULID per batch, reused on retry), `User-Agent` from `userAgent()`, NO `Authorization` header; any outcome (204, error, timeout 5 s) is silent to the user, logged at debug without payload; no retries beyond re-queueing the batch once.
scope_out: The opt-in prompt UI and `centcom telemetry on|off|reset|status` command wiring: CLI/TUI lanes (this lane exposes functions).
Deciding where events are emitted in other lanes: those lanes call these functions.
build_against: Mock backend (lane C007) accepts `POST /v1/telemetry/events` and returns 204; frames are captured in its request log for assertions. Unit tests use a fake HTTP transport, fake clock and in-memory fs.
interfaces: `createTelemetry(deps: { config: () => { enabled: boolean }; env: Env; clock: Clock; fs: StateFs; http: HttpPost; ids: IdGenerator; log: Logger; ua: string; baseUrl: string }): Telemetry`

`interface Telemetry { appStart(): void; appExit(): void; commandRun(name: string): void; sessionCreated(mode: 'command_post'|'branch', transport: 'lan'|'relay'): void; sessionJoined(transport: 'lan'|'relay'): void; agentStateChange(from: AgentWireState, to: AgentWireState): void; featureUsed(key: string): void; errorShown(code: ErrorCode): void; perfStartup(ms: number): void; perfFrame(p95Ms: number): void; updateResult(from: string, to: string, ok: boolean): void; flush(deadlineMs?: number): Promise<void>; resetInstallId(): Promise<void>; status(): TelemetryStatus }`
Wire event shape is taken from the generated telemetry type in `@centcom/protocol`.
acceptance: With default config (`telemetry.enabled=false`) 10,000 emit calls produce zero HTTP requests, zero files written and no timers started.
`DO_NOT_TRACK=1` with `telemetry.enabled=true` still sends nothing; so does `CENTCOM_TELEMETRY=off`.
Enabled: 250 events emitted within 1 s produce exactly 3 batches of 100, 100, 50 (first sent immediately, the next two respecting the 60 s gap using the fake clock); no batch exceeds 64 KiB.
Emitting 1,200 events while the network is down leaves exactly 1,000 buffered and the oldest 200 dropped.

`commandRun('foo bar')`, `featureUsed('/home/alex/x')`, `errorShown('not_a_code')` are dropped and `status().dropped` increments; no payload contains path-like strings, branch names, e-mail addresses or hostnames (property test with planted canaries).

Requests carry `Idempotency-Key` matching the CT-IDS/UUID rule (<= 64 chars), the same key on the single re-queue, and contain no `Authorization`, cookie or `usr_`/`mem_`/`dev_`/`ses_` id anywhere in the body.
`resetInstallId()` produces a different ULID and the old one is gone from disk.
A 500 or timeout (5 s) never throws or prints to stdout/stderr, and `flush(2000)` always resolves within 2000 ms.
tests: gate.test.ts (config x env matrix), allowlist.test.ts (valid/invalid per event).
guardrails: MUST be off by default and MUST honour `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` and `CENTCOM_TELEMETRY=off` unconditionally, even over an explicit config value.

MUST NEVER include message/code/diff text, paths, branch or repo names, prompts, model output, hostnames, usernames, e-mails, keys or ciphertext (CT-TELEMETRY rule 1); the event API accepts only enums, bounded ints and registry names.
MUST NOT send an Authorization header or any user/device/session id; `install_id` MUST NOT be derived from user data.
MUST NOT block startup, exit or any user action on telemetry; all I/O is fire-and-forget with a 5 s cap and a 2 s exit flush.
MUST NOT persist events to disk (only `install_id`); a crash loses at most the in-memory buffer.
failure_modes: Backend unreachable or 4xx/5xx -> batch re-queued once then dropped; user sees nothing.
State dir unwritable -> `install_id` kept in memory for the process, telemetry still works, one debug log.
Clock jumps backwards -> send gap measured with a monotonic source; never sends faster than once per 60 s.
